newsitem.title: GERMANY: Kohl says too soon to decide on solidarity tax.
newsitem.headline: Kohl says too soon to decide on solidarity tax.

text.p: German Chancellor Helmut Kohl said on Thursday it was too soon to set a date for the elimination of the unpopular solidarity tax surcharge.
Kohl told a news conference the decision could be made only after more was known about how the planned comprehensive tax reform would develop.
The surcharge on income taxes, designed to help finance the reconstruction of east Germany, is due to be cut to 5.5 percent from the current 7.5 percent next year.
Kohl's Free Democrat coalition partners have been pressing for a commitment to eliminate the tax by the year 2000.
